solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food shop just opened covering Hungary's capital city

parts.note: something just opened is new

indicators.note: the shop's name is wrapped around the next piece, covering it

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods
H is the international vehicle registration letter for Hungary

explanation.surface: A newly opened delicatessen stocks goods from Budapest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hungary's capital' looks like Budapest, but 'capital city' is the definition, and Hungary only gives H, which 'covering' puts inside DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian seat of government is located in this city, making it a national capital.

clue.text: Trouble in dive, doing a somersault — snatched

indicators.note: placed inside the next piece
turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a seedy haunt, like a dive
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A diver somersaults badly, then something is grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' is a noun here, a seedy haunt, and it is the dive that somersaults to read NED before the trouble goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed is slang for caught or seized, as when police nail a suspect.

clue.text: Pest's not great, not nice, not finished

parts.note: wee means small

indicators.note: incomplete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: vile means nasty

explanation.surface: A pest that is small, nasty and unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts the E off VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a beetle that damages grain and crops, a classic agricultural pest.

clue.text: They're not really what you see at the movies

definitions.text: They're not really what you see at the movies

parts.words: They're not really what you see at the movies
parts.note: special film illusions, simulated events that are not real

explanation.surface: A remark that what appears on screen is illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Special effects are cinematic illusions created to simulate things that are not actually there.

clue.text: Hard test around start of last month virtually completely relating to computer characters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the test word goes round the date

parts.note: an exam is a test
the first day of the year's last month, December 1st, written DEC I

indicators.note: almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means completely

explanation.surface: A tough exam held near the start of December, almost entirely about computers.
explanation.walkthrough: The start of the last month is its first day, 1 December, written with the Roman numeral I; 'virtually' drops a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexadecimal is base sixteen notation, used in computing to represent bytes and character codes.

clue.text: Article recalled English in America showing feeling of disgust

indicators.note: called back, so the word for the article is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: 'an' is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the abbreviation for English sits inside the one for America

parts.note: USA, the United States of America

explanation.surface: Somebody remembers an English article in the US that disgusted them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like remembering, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness, and figuratively the queasy revulsion that something repugnant provokes.

clue.text: US state following President's lead? Not his lead

indicators.note: without his first letter, so the O at the start of the surname goes

parts.note: following the lead of the then President would be 'à la Obama'

explanation.surface: A US state copying the President, but not in everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'à la' means in the manner of; 'Not his lead' removes the O from OBAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the southern states of America.

clue.text: She's primarily brazen item?

indicators.note: first of all, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: a trumpet is made of brass, so it is literally brazen

explanation.surface: A question about a woman who is shameless above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brazen' means both made of brass and shameless, so the whole clue also defines a brazen woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old insulting word for a promiscuous or shameless woman.

clue.text: Sound one's Hs, as with Hook?

parts.note: Captain Hook, the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A question whether Captain Hook pronounces his aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate is to pronounce a breathy initial h sound, as in 'house' rather than ''ouse'.

clue.text: Backed cut-down outlet to supply current? Nothing else comes to mind

indicators.note: moving backwards, so the whole assembled string is read from right to left
shortened, so the word for outlet loses its final letter

parts.note: an exit is a way out
to feed is to supply, as with power
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An electrician's puzzle about a shortened socket being used to supply power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-down' trims EXIT to EXI; with FEED and I that makes EXIFEEDI, which 'Backed' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An idée fixe is an obsession, a single thought that dominates and crowds out all others.

clue.text: Corporal punishment drawing in American tyrant

indicators.note: pulling something inside, so the strap encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a strap was a leather belt used to beat pupils, so the word stands for corporal punishment

explanation.surface: Physical punishment attracts an American despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a Persian provincial governor, and by extension any despotic subordinate ruler.

clue.text: Demonstrated Northern church's involvement in regressive bar

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it, so the pair go into the reversed bar
going backwards, so the word for the bar is read in reverse

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone showed a northern church's connection to a backward drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' reads as a political or moral word, but here it just means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal clearly, a straight synonym of displayed.

clue.text: Language rules, good rules about form of 'to be', viewed from all sides?

indicators.note: the pair of rule letters surround the next piece

parts.note: R stands for a rule or ruler (rex/regina); two of them make RR

parts.words: form of 'to be', viewed from all sides
parts.note: 'am' is a form of the verb to be; seen from both directions it is AM followed by its reversal MA

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson discussing the rules for the verb 'to be'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewed from all sides' means AM is read forwards and then backwards, AMMA, which 'about' puts between the two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is the set of rules governing how a language is structured and used.

clue.text: Gets me a suit tailored for a rather dodgy figure

indicators.note: cut and altered to fit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man getting a suit made to flatter a dubious physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like body shape but means a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesstimate is a rough estimate, a number arrived at by partly guessing.

clue.text: Most of islander information snatched by determined spy

indicators.note: taken hold of by, so the next pieces sit inside the word for determined

parts.note: set, as in set on doing something

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Cretan is an inhabitant of the island of Crete
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy grabs most of the intelligence from an islander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'information' is GEN, British slang as in 'get the gen'; 'Most of' drops only the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is an undercover operative gathering intelligence, the plain meaning of a spy.

clue.text: Trainee's supported by alien communication set-up

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an intern is a trainee on work placement
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A trainee is helped by an alien to set up communications.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet is the global network linking computers for exchanging messages and data.

clue.text: Weapon carrier travels by water, turning up right in blockade of river

indicators.note: in a down answer, upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: someone who rows travels by boat

indicators.note: placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a dam blocks a river

explanation.surface: A boat trip upriver turns back at a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-arm is the arm that wields a blade, so it carries the weapon.

clue.text: Cues Enigma Variations around start of week for ambient sounds

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed round the following letter
variations are altered versions, so these letters are rearranged
the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A music note: Elgar's Enigma Variations giving cues around the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variations' rearranges CUES ENIGMA, and 'around' puts that around W, the start of 'week'. Elgar's Enigma Variations is a famous orchestral work, which makes the anagram signal look like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: New age music is gentle, atmospheric instrumental music designed to relax, i.e. ambient sound.

clue.text: Lively appreciation of music including piano? One's not studying now

indicators.note: taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: gay in its old sense of merry and lively
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an ear for music is an appreciation of it

explanation.surface: A cheerful musical ear, piano included; someone takes time off study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lively' uses the old sense of gay, merry; the piano letter goes inside that word, not the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap year is a break, usually between school and university, spent away from formal study.

clue.text: Liniment affected head of runner initially

parts.note: camp means exaggerated or affected in manner

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A rub that affected a runner's head first.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a strong-smelling compound used in rubs and ointments for aches.

clue.text: Composer's candid about origin of composition

indicators.note: the honest word goes round the single letter

parts.note: frank means candid

indicators.note: the start, so the first letter

explanation.surface: A composer is being honest about where a piece of music came from.
explanation.walkthrough: César Franck was a Belgian-born French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: César Franck wrote the Symphony in D minor and much organ music.

clue.text: The French facing their vote against accepting new or old pop star

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: taking in, so the vote surrounds the letter

parts.note: non is French for no, so it is the French vote against

explanation.surface: French voters reject a pop star, new or old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to the French, so the vote is their 'non'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon of the Beatles was a hugely famous musician of the 1960s and 70s.

clue.text: Run back to gather our various widely-spread crime-fighters

indicators.note: to gather in, so the reversed word encloses the rearranged letters
the word for run is read backwards

parts.note: to lope is to run with long strides

indicators.note: in various forms, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Instructions to run back and round up our assorted police forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is a verb meaning lope, not the answer's start.
explanation.definitionFit: Europol is the European Union's law-enforcement agency, coordinating policing across many countries.

clue.text: Losing head, shows a little passion before energy dip

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter

parts.note: someone who simmers is quietly seething, showing a little passion
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper slightly before taking an energising dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' takes the S off SIMMERS to leave IMMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse something is to plunge it into liquid, which is what dipping does.

clue.text: Trim end of curtain attacked by moths

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word

parts.note: moth-eaten fabric has been eaten by moths

explanation.surface: Cutting off the end of a curtain that moths have damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to tidy up, and trim as a verb means making tidy by cutting.

clue.text: Exploit deception involving a bit of leg

indicators.note: taking in, so the word for deception wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
the shin is the front part of the leg below the knee

explanation.surface: A scam involving a glimpse of leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in on something is to take advantage of it for profit, i.e. to make use of it.

clue.text: Doctor probing flag's colour we hear

indicators.note: investigating from inside, so the doctor goes into the word for flag

parts.note: to flag is to tire
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor examines the colour of a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colour we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is the definition: tone colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tonal quality of a sound, often called tone colour by musicians.

clue.text: Newspaper department's popular, snapping Queen in leather

indicators.note: grabbing hold of, so the department encloses the royal abbreviation

parts.note: a desk is a section of a newspaper, e.g. the news desk
ER, Elizabeth Regina
in, as in fashionable

explanation.surface: A newspaper desk is popular for its photograph of the Queen in leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapping' looks like photography but means seizing; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskin is hide from a deer, a soft kind of tanned animal skin.
